name: computational-research
description: AI-assisted computational research with every generated file landing in an Artifacts folder under one dated stem while everything outside one stays the user's, license-aware MCP-first Wolfram execution, wiki knowledge base, LaTeX/Typst paper scaffolding, Wolfram paclet development in which each exported function is written to stand alone, publishable to the Function Repository unchanged, mathematical objects defined as inert heads that compute only when read in a structure, code conventions shared with the PureMath style guide, one house layout for Wolfram code shipped to every project (spaced brackets, chained With, the body on its own line, no comments) with a graphics style that reads in light and dark mode, notebook content rules and the [[ LLM Generated ]] subtitle on every generated notebook, symbol-page documentation bundled and publicly deployed on publish, dual-engine Markdown-to-notebook conversion that auto-detects a pinned rich converter for frontmatter/LaTeX-math sources, notebook generation including research notebooks written as ordinary mathematics papers under a writing guide shared with the LaTeX/Typst scaffolder (the body carries only settled statements, proved in full or cited to a source that was read; experiments gathered near the end rather than in the development and everything below the settled tier handed to the journal so nothing is dropped; complete gap-free prose proofs, never abbreviated to fit and never shattered into tiny lemmas; one example per statement, definitions included, answering with a geometry illustration that shows the phenomenon — erring large rather than small, and carrying no labels — or one small algebraic value, its code folded and its bare graphic not; explicit length budgets; each result stated at the generality its proof actually reaches rather than hedged wider, statements naming their own hypotheses so they lift out intact, and conjectures or questions saying what would settle them, gathered in an outlook rather than left where they arose; the model as sole author, the footnote naming the operator, summarising the instructions and disclosing in bold how much freedom the model had — Directed, Guided or Open exploration; statements, equations and sections numbered by the front end and cited by tag, so no number is ever typed into the source) built by the rich converter plus MathNotebook post-processing on the structure-only PlainArticle stylesheet that keeps Default typography (numbered environments converted through folded cell groups, citations, one-way generation with fingerprint-based drift detection), guided tours, Wolfram ecosystem search, pure-math project scaffolding with MathWorld/nLab/OEIS/DLMF/Wikipedia search, BibTeX from arXiv/DOI, Lean/Mathlib formalization bridge, multi-session work tracking on a measured item format that opens like a GitHub issue (summary, motivation, acceptance criteria and prompt history for the human, technical details and tasks for the sessions; hand-off/decisions, one-line-per-session progress, one-fact-one-destination), a backlog refined together with the user until it is ready, per-task test instructions and a review folder before an item counts as done, a private web board of all items, readable and editable from a phone, whose queued edits, approvals and notes reach the files on a manual sync, with an in-session orchestrator (autolab) that works ready items from a chat, one watchable, steerable background worker per task in its own worktree, and a headless driver for cron that works ready items unattended one cold session per task, routing each task to the model tier and reasoning effort its own annotation names and reporting the tier it used, verifying each run, allowlisting the Wolfram MCP by default, and landing work on a review branch, Conventional-Commits enforcement via scaffolded git hooks, optional prompt-provenance tracking for generated artifacts, an optional cited scientific journal (def/thm/rem) in LaTeX/Typst, a per-project one-sentence-per-line source-formatting toggle, and a revision workflow in which the user reviews inside the document — notes written as << … >> and direct edits, in any notebook or paper — and each round writes the next numbered version beside the last, changing only what was asked, while a provenance file beside the document remembers every note with the lines it was about, every hand edit and every chat request, and keeps the rules drawn from them so a correction is needed once; generated notebooks stay out of git and their Markdown source is committed instead; earlier rounds move to an Archive folder on request.
